risks: Reviews were not independent: the orchestrator session did the work and accepted it. Fine for a connectivity test, not for real tickets.
Claude Code drove the server through an ad-hoc MCP client script; the darkmechanicus server is not yet registered as an MCP server in Claude Code, so agents in a normal session do not see the tools.
Host catalog lists models without context windows (unknown, left null).

content.summary: Sprint 1 confirmed the full MCP loop from an external agent host (Claude Code) against the installed v0.8.0 app. A planner session created the epic and both tickets as a draft; a person saved revision 1 and queued the run in the desktop. An orchestrator session registered a host catalog, picked up the queued run, and claimed, submitted, and accepted DM-1 then DM-2 in dependency order. Both tickets were verification-only and changed no repository files. Nothing failed or is blocked.
